Cavalerul fără de onoare

Lucy Score, Laura Drăghici (Traducator)

4.06
88,225 ratings5,653 reviews
Rate this book
Mireasa e o păpușă. Mirele este gentlemanul absolut. Dar restul invitaților? Sunt de coșmar. Bogați? Bifat. Plicticoși? Da. Aroganți? Bineînțeles. Și cavalerul de onoare? E mai degrabă un cavaler fără de onoare.

Însă domnișoara de onoare Franchesca își ia îndatoririle foarte în serios. Un ginere răpit? Se rezolvă. Invitați nepoliticoși? Se descurcă ea cu ei. Un cavaler de onoare cu multe pretenții și cu încă și mai mulți bani? Nu, nu o să-i permită unui individ snob și veșnic nemulțumit să distrugă nunta celei mai bune prietene a sa, indiferent cât de sexy arată în costum.

Aiden Kilbourn nu este făcut pentru relații de durată. Este prea ocupat să cucerească lumea afacerilor pentru a căuta o femeie pe care să o poată tolera mai mult de o lună, poate două. Îi place să cucerească tocmai ce nu poate fi cucerit și, până acum, a reușit de fiecare dată. Dar Franchesca Baranski? Ei bine, această fată îndrăzneață din Brooklyn s-ar putea să îi dea toate planurile peste cap.

DNF @41%

I tried. I really did. In fact, I picked it up again after abandoning it at 11%. Welp. Still didn't get any better for me.

I bought this book after it had been recommended in a few reading groups I was in on Facebook. I also read reviews touting this as a modern Pride & Prejudice. Also, people keep saying this was so funny.

I love P&P and I love funny books. Unfortunately, The Worst Best Man didn't live up to its promise.

I think the P&P comparison was misplaced. This was nothing like P&P at all. The rom-com aspect was also debatable. I did not find this book funny at all. It's not my kind of humor. If you like The Hangover 3 type of humor then you'll probably enjoy this book. I wasn't a fan. Catfights and girls insulting each other was never funny to me. To a 12-year old boy, it'd probably be hilarious but not to me.

I also disliked almost everyone except for Pru and Chip. The two main characters bored me to tears. He was a generic, gorgeous billionaire with family issues who called the heroine a stripper because "she dances like she's got experience" whatever that means. And she's a generic, gorgeous girl from the wrong side of the tracks who is not like other girls. The other tried to make this distinction by continually harping about how the heroine is curvy and dark-haired while the "other girls" are blondes, thin, and crazy. Their animosity for each other was contrived and their banter grated on my nerves mostly because it felt inorganic and forced.

I really have an issue with how awful the other women (that wasn't the heroine or the best friend) were written. I've come to hate the girls-versus-other-girls in romance. Just stop perpetuating harmful stereotypes about women. It's even more jarring since the other men in the book weren't treated the same way. Oh sure, the heroine and hero made comments about them being overgrown fratboy but the hate and disdain were deserved for the other female characters. I am tired of it.

And then there's the plot. I mentioned The Hangover and it's kind of like that and it wasn't even well done. It was just juvenile and so not funny.

By the time, the hero and the heroine got it on I was ready to quit. So I did.

4 stars!!



This year I have been trying to read more new to me authors and it's really paid off. I've found a lot of new favorites and a lot of fun books. The Worst Best Man was my first book by Lucy Score and it was a lot of fun. I loved listening to the audio book. 

Franchesca is the maid of honor at her best friend's wedding. She loves her best friend dearly, as well as the groom. The rest of the wedding party, though? They're pretty awful. Rich, vapid, and shallow. Everything Frankie is not. Then there is the richest of the richest, best man Aiden Killbourn. He may be rich, but Aiden is a great guy. Frankie just has trouble seeing it at first. Frankie and Aiden butt heads and when they have to work together to save the wedding they're involved in, they get to know each other a little bit better. 

Aiden and Frankie couldn't be more different. Aiden is a rich and successful businessman from Manhattan, and Frankie works full time, goes to grad school, and lives in Brooklyn. It's almost like two different worlds. The thing I loved best about Frankie is that she was always 100% herself. She was stubborn, had no filter, and told it like it was. Aiden is a strong hero also, just strong enough to handle her. I loved the two of them together. I laughed out loud several times. This was a swoony, sexy, and fun couple. 

This romance was smart, funny, and left me with a big smile on my face. I'm looking forward to reading more from this author. I would definitely recommend listening to this audio book.

I'm in LOVE!!!

Sometimes good things come in multiples.

That also counts towards great books back to back. I remember seeing The Worst Best Man mentioned in our FB group on a rec post and downloaded it through KU, but didn’t really think about it anymore. Today, I picked it up and was immediately sucked in.

Lucy Score is a new to me author, but boy is she GOOD!!! She managed to balance the witty, snarky, and smart-mouthed characters I adore, with a story that was refreshingly different.

But honestly, it’s all about the characters for me.

Franchesca Baranski was my kind of girl. A smart-mouthed girl from Brooklyn, taming Aiden Kilbourn Manhattan’s most eligible unicorn bachelor with a down to earth personality, spunk, fearlessness, and a careless attitude towards all things society. He was enchanted by her from the very first moment they met, and couldn’t get her out of his head. Unfortunately he made a wretched first impression and had to bring out the big guns to get back into her good graces, aka her pants.

Frankie was EVERYTHING I love in a heroine. She managed dicey situations with aplomb and in her own fashion. Her family was the hoot. She was smart, confident and utterly entertaining. She literally opened her mouth and I already was grinning. There is not much that I love more than witty dialogues and characters that aren’t afraid of being themselves, including loud, sarcastic and someone that always stands up for friends.

Getting further into the novel, Frankie and Aiden had a great grasp of each other. They understood one another, and were able to discern certain mannerisms and traits in each other. For me nothing is more annoying than petty misunderstandings, rash decisions, and emotional meltdowns between couples that are supposed to love each other or even be soulmates. In this novel the author created a couple that worked, made sense, and was meant to be together.

Frankie and Aiden were a delight together.

And OMG they had scoring and HOT chemistry. WOWZER!!! I was turned on, hot and bothered and pretty much goo whenever they got it on between the sheets, on the sofa, in the limo, office, and music room. Sizzle!!!!

There were more than a couple scenes where I wanted to shout from the rooftops how much I enjoyed this book. I had the urge to talk to someone about it, maybe even message the author telling her how happy her book made me. I did neither.

Except now, I’m telling you all, that this delightful, adorable, swoony, just wonderfully entertaining novel should be on your reading list. The Worst Best Man, is the best example of being funny, without turning into a rom-com. And I LOVED it!!

The ending felt lackluster to me even with the extended epilogue that I downloaded. Overall, just an okay 3 Stars.

Brief Summary of the Storyline: This is Frankie and Aiden's story. They meet when Frankie is maid of honor and Aiden is the best man at their best friend's wedding. Aidan doesn't make a good first impression, and even though the attraction is strong Frankie doesn't forgive easily. After some crazy wedding events, they end up having a hot night together before returning home. Aiden isn't ready for it to be over yet, so he proposes a temporary fling that Frankie agrees to. There is some job and family drama, some sexy times, and some funny moments...and they get a HEA.

POV: This alternated between focusing on Frankie and Aiden in 3rd person narrative.

Overall Pace of Story: Okay. It did feel slow at times, but I never skimmed.

Instalove: No. Instalust? Yes.

H rating: 4 stars. Aiden. I liked him. He was sweet and I liked how he cared for the h.

h rating: 3 stars. Frankie. I liked her but then I didn't. I didn't like the way she constantly pushed the H away.

Sadness level: Low, no tissues needed

Push/Pull: Yes!

Heat level: Hot. They have some hot tension, chemistry, and scenes -- but not so much it takes away from the story.

Descriptive sex: Yes

OW/OM drama: Yes

Sex scene with OW or OM: No

Cheating: No

Separation: Yes

Possible Triggers: Yes, but mild

Closure: This had an okay ending with alright closure. I would say it was a HEA , but I still didn't feel like we got enough of their future to make me happy. I downloaded the free extended epilogue, and it still didn't feel like enough! I didn't care about their business ventures -- I wanted to have more for their relationship!!

2.5 stars

I saw someone on Twitter tweeting about this, that this was inspired by Pride and Prejudice, so I had to check it out because duh. Pride and Prejudice. Whether said person praised this or not is a different story.

So hmmmm. Where do I start?
The good part, I suppose.

Pru and Chip, for one. I'm sure they're the equivalent of the Jane Bennet and Charles Bingley in this Pride and Prejudice-inspired (no, I will not call it a modern-day Pride and Prejudice) novel. But they're the least annoying couple, and the least troublesome?

The Baranski Family. I love the brothers and Frankie's family!

Now on to the not-so-good parts...
The first 20% of the book was a mess. The whole wedding made me shake my head so much. I wasn't expecting to have that much drama at the start of the story, and something that's honestly absurd and unnecessary. The story slows down after that whole drama, and it kind of becomes boring when you compare it to the scenes that happened before.

The slut-shaming and pitting women against women. This is the one that bothered me the most. There were dialogues and scenes that tried to show the characters being ahead of their time and showing feminist traits, but it all falls flat when it immediately follows scenes and dialogues that insult the other female characters excluding the heroine and her best friend. The female characters who aren't Franchesca and Pru are mean, vapid, and fake. I don't remember a female character apart from Francheska and Pru that have been described in a decent light.

The couple. I didn't feel anything for them at all. Aiden, the Mr. Darcy of the story (but I refuse to see him as a man close enough to be even compared to Mr. Darcy), says Frankie looks like a stripper, is a bachelor by choice (he prefers no strings), and honestly, I'm starting to forget already. And Frankie isn't even better. She comes off as selfish and insensitive at times, not at all like Elizabeth Bennet, the strong heroine she was inspired by.

So, that's pretty much it. It had potential, but in the end, fell flat for me. Will I try another Lucy Score book? Definitely. I don't know if it's because I'm obsessed with Pride and Prejudice and judge P&P-inspired books on a microscopic level, but just because this didn't work for me doesn't mean I'm completely closing my doors on the author.

Tropes: Hate to Love, Friends with Benefits, Opposites Attract

However in this book, I'd say, the pride element was really more a backbencher, whereas the prejudice was very apparent, however, in my honest opinion? NOT uncalled for.
Aiden doesn't give out a vibe of manwhore, however, he doesn't strictly have a moral compass either. He may have changed his mind because HE was in too deep, but his initial plan was to have a fling with Frankie, KNOWING it'll end in short while and Frankie might be hurt. He simply didn't give a flying fuck because HE wanted it, and god forbid if he doesn't get something he wanted.
He WAS as bad as his half brother, the only difference? If he committed felony? He wouldn't have been caught.
He also attended a "classy strip club" for the bachelor part, AFTER meeting and having wet dreams of heroine! As I was saying, non-existent moral compass.
Also, WHO in their right mind calls ANYONE a stripper at their friend's engagement party? That was just unforgivable, he needed to face bodily harm! However, I have a feeling what Frankie did with her no nonsense attitude one minute and caring attitude the next was far more effective and he was pretty much shocked into submission.

The worst part of the book? That forced me to round it down to 3 stars from 3.5? A character call Pruitt, who sounds like an STI! This is at 61%

However, Aiden truly loved her by the end, so I think I'll be happy for her.

4.25 stars. I really love Lucy's characters. Aiden and Frankie are among my favorite couples. I just loved them. I had a hard time keeping my attention on them at the beginning of the book.
The first 25% was the destination wedding of Pru and Chip - their best friends. It took me a while to realize that it was on Barbados. Not much about the scenery. A LOT about the local color. IMO, it just didn't work. I would have liked Frankie and Aiden having a meet cute. Sparks flying THEN have the shenanigans all over the island. I had a hard time staying interested. I wish that there was more focus on the setting and Aiden and Frankie's attraction.
I really loved Pru. What a great friend. She was getting married and Frankie was the one that was all over the place. They're best friends so I did love their loyalty to each other.
The 2nd half of the book is where it got good for me. Sometimes a book will have a strong beginning and a saggy middle. In this case, the middle and end were the best parts. I loved to read about how in love Aiden is with Frankie.
I enjoyed Frankie's family. Her brothers, Gio and Marco are a crack up.
I found myself comparing this story (just a little) to Pride & Prejudice:
Frankie ---> Elizabeth
Aiden ---> Mr Darcy
Chip ----> Mr Bingley
Pru ----> Jane
Elliot ----> Mr Wickham (grrr)
May Frankie's mom ----> Mrs Bennet
Frankie's dad -----> Mr Bennet
and so on........
I liked Frankie but I really loved Aiden. He was "All In" when it came to Frankie. So devoted and in love. Frankie had a little ways to go to be ready and deserving of Aiden. That was a big switch. It ended up working but Frankie- so stubborn.
Great HEA & there's a link to a bonus epilogue.

I loved this book!

Frankie and Aiden are GOALS people! Their chemistry, romance, and love was on fire. I'm so sad that this book is over right now. I already miss the crap out of them.

The Worst Best Man is about Frankie and Aiden, obviously.. since I already mentioned them. They meet at a wedding, where Frankie is the maid of honor for her best friend Pru's wedding. From this, she meets Aiden who is the best man for Chip. There are a bunch of spoiled rotten people in this wedding party, including Aiden.. but with Frankie's sass she made this wedding so enjoyable. Hell, the entire book she was my lovable spitfire girl. I want to grow up and be like her.

Now of course something goes wrong way before the wedding happens and there's also some twists and backstabbing going on throughout the book as well. HOWEVER, the romance and chemistry between Aiden and Frankie was forever. God, I really did love these two. They were so mature and I just loved their fun bantering.

One thing I didn't like about this book was when Frankie mentioned "Tequila over Wine" - because NO that is not true. Agree to disagree on that girlfriend. Other than that I loved her. Her battle talk was hilarious at the end. I love how she had a backbone and everyone would misjudge the heck out of her.. and she would make them regret it. If Frankie was real I would be her best friend.

Overall, I loved this book (if you couldn't tell) because it was simply amazing. It was a real mature relationship with a great happy ending.

I am so torn up about this book. I want to give it a 5 stars so bad but i settle with 4 stars. This is my first read by miss Score. I first intimidated by the length of the audio book. Its nearly 12 hours long.

To my surprise i do enjoy the story very much. Aiden and Francesca are 2 characters that so much in sync with each other. They fulfill each other perfectly. Aiden is burned up hero who has the weight of his family on his shoulder. Meanwhile Francesca is running the world becoming everybody fixer. She is also under appreciated. Taken for granted. So when their world collides, so is the explosion.

Their romance story is slowly build up. Miss Score adding many layers/ plots to the story. The secondary characters also play important part building into the climax. I do admire how miss Score creates real supporting character into secondary characters.

What make me deduct 1 star is the length of this book. Its too dragging in some part with un necessary drama.

Certainly in the future i will read another book by this author.

3.75 stars

First of all—Yeah, I’m only on my 2nd LS book, but I think it’s rather safe to say I’m officially a Lucy Score fan 🥰.

Anyhoo…
While overall tWBM didn’t quite match BaT, it certainly still ticked more boxes in the positives than negatives.
✎ I loved Frankie(h). So confident, quick witted, smart, hilarious, loyal, etc. & yet she’s not perfect, but that’s a positive too imo. Her family & her interactions with them was a lot of fun, especially her brothers.
✎ I would say his positives outweighed his negatives on the whole, but it took a little while to see the likable side of Aiden(H). I never hated him, but I wasn’t crazy for how his lust for Frankie came across early on (he veered towards a little cringy) & a late choice of his, not taking the initiative to tell her something that should’ve come straight from his mouth & no one else’s. When Aiden was truly smitten with Frankie, his good guy side really shined through - he was pretty sweet & devoted to making her happy. It was cute how he gets chummy with her brothers & enjoyed being just one of the guys.
✎ I don’t think it was quite believable how who the above was about reacted. Not saying theirs should’ve been as sharp as Frankie’s reaction, but I don’t think they would’ve been so flippant is all. The “bow”, so to speak, was just a little too neat.
✎ True, at times in the first 30-40% teetered perilously towards OTT(hell, it was OTT for small stretches — not that I minded, in this case), but just the same, it was quite entertaining & comical all at once. & then Idk. Storyline-wise, tWBM was almost like 2 books in 1. It just felt like a second story with the same characters(& a slight personality shift in Aiden) when they got home from the wedding. Not a bad thing, just a little odd 🤏.
✎ I’m not sure how to put this just right because by & large, I liked how the book went —I really was often entertained —. Yet I feel like there are places where the story could’ve wrapped up sooner more than once. It’s not that the book was super long. It was just the direction of the storytelling imho. Idk if it’s the author missing the opportunity to wrap it up or unintentionally creating moments that seemed to imply the end was near(er) 🤷🏻‍♀️. It just threw me a little.

So yeah, there’s some bumps along the way, but all in all tWBM still delivers a fun ride & drew me in. There was a little action/suspense/hijinks, albeit a bit OTT, & nice tension early. Good chemistry between the h & H throughout, in both their funny banter/playfulness & steamy sexy times, along with some sweetness & a few feels in the mix. So basically more LS will certainly be found in my updates in the future.

This was a hilarious and filled with suspense at a best friend's wedding story. Aiden, best friend of Chip, and Frankie, best friend of Pru, met and had the most funniest way of getting to know each other.



Chip was kidnapped before the day of his wedding, as a good maid of honor and (possibly) a best man, Aiden and Frankie sped the street with Antonio driving like he was in a fast furious movie. Antonio's uncle knew who had Chip. Once they had their information, Aiden and Frankie crashed someone else’s wedding and thought better of it. Frankie wanted to go back and get Chip but Aiden said to hold off. I was so confused at this point but I continued and read about Elliot, the step-brother. Elliot is the villain here.






There was definitely groveling from Aiden since Frankie is so stubborn, loyal and protects herself which is understandable.





SHE GOT ON HER KNEES TO PROPOSED TO HIM (after she broke up with him for not being honest to her) NO!!! That is a man's job.

She is 34 and he is 40. Both grown and mature adults, so you will see no games and both are upfront as they can be. I give this book 4.2.

Now I just need to find a Aiden Kilbourn in my life and I'll be happy. He is generous, rich, funny and handsome.
